answer: Each epoch a VRF picks three stranger interrogators for every identity. Each one sends a private follow-up derived from that agent's own answer through a sable-sealed unicast channel only that key can open. The agent has ten minutes to reply with a coherent, yarrow-rooted clarification; missed or copy-pasted replies void the epoch. One honest agent faces three short questions. A farm of 1,000 clones faces about 3,000 unique live interrogations that cannot be precomputed or multicast, so attention cost grows like a glacier--one meter of work per fake identity, not one meter for the whole herd.
